name: Couchbase, Inc.
origin_detail: Created in February 2011 by merging Membase, Inc. (founded 2009 as NorthScale by memcached leaders James Phillips, Steve Yen and Dustin Sallings) with CouchOne (founded 2009 as Relaxed in Berkeley, whose people had major roles in Apache CouchDB). Wikipedia lists the HQ as San Jose, California (the page is internally inconsistent).
openness_notes: Couchbase Server shipped as an Apache-2.0 Community Edition (without recent bug fixes) alongside a commercial Enterprise Edition, i.e. open core (2). On 2021-03-26 Couchbase announced it was adopting the Business Source License 1.1; Wikipedia now lists BSL 1.1 and calls the software source-available, so the current level is 1. Which versions moved and whether older code stays Apache-2.0 was not confirmed.

license_history.note: 'Couchbase Adopts BSL License', Couchbase blog, 2021-03-26, cited by Wikipedia (the blog itself returned HTTP 403).

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Came four months before the IPO. No fork appears in the fetched sources.

exit_events.note: Listed 2021-07-21 (Wikipedia). Priced at $24.00; 9,589,999 shares including the fully exercised over-allotment; ~$230M gross proceeds (Baird deal card). IPO valuation not confirmed.

Definitive agreement 2025-06-20 at $24.50/share cash, a 29% premium to the 2025-06-18 close and 67% to the 2025-03-27 close; Haveli already owned 9.6%. Completed 2025-09-24; stock delisted from Nasdaq; Matt Cain stayed as CEO.

risk_events: 2025-03-27: Share price low enough that the later $24.50 offer was a 67% premium
robustness: Single vendor with no foundation and no known fork; owned by private equity (Haveli) since September 2025. Apache CouchDB, an ASF project, shares only history with it.
openness_effect_assessment: An Apache-licensed open core carried Couchbase to a 2021 Nasdaq IPO at $24 a share, but it switched to BSL just before listing and never re-rated: private equity bought it in 2025 for $24.50 a share (~$1.5B), almost exactly the IPO price. The closing triggered no fork, probably because no large third party was reselling it, but it also bought no visible valuation gain.
key_takeaway: Couchbase is the private-equity version of the consolidation that IBM drove with HashiCorp and Confluent: a smaller open-core database that moved to BSL in 2021, stayed flat in public markets, and was taken private by Haveli Investments for about $1.5B in September 2025, at roughly its IPO price.

sources.title: Couchbase agrees to be acquired by private equity firm Haveli for $1.5B
